deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page continues the previous one. Gauss is designing a telescope with four thin lenses: an objective and three eyepiece lenses. He uses his own 1841 'Dioptrische Untersuchungen' formalism. The objective is common to all trials (1/862). The previous page tried other separations; this page is a further trial with separations 700, 123.3, 5.8.

(1) DATA. The left column gives the lens powers as fractions: phi1 = 1/862, phi2 = 1/181.8, phi3 = 1/97.3, phi4 = 1/67.3. The right column gives the separations d1 = 700, d2 = 123.3, d3 = 5.8.

(2) RAY RECURSION. Two independent paraxial rays are traced through the system. The recursion below is my reconstruction; it reproduces every entry to the last digit.
- Ray 1 (the axial ray from the distant object) is the pair (alpha_k, beta_k).
- Ray 2 (the ray through the objective centre) is the pair (gamma_k, delta_k).
- At each step, with the sign alternation Gauss uses:
  alpha_{k+1} = d_{k+1}*beta_k - alpha_k,
  beta_{k+1} = alpha_{k+1}*phi_{k+2} - beta_k,
  and the same rules for (gamma, delta).
- Start values: alpha = 1, beta = phi1 = 0.001160; gamma = 0, delta = 1.
- Ray 1:
  alpha' = 700*0.00116 - 1 = -0.1879;
  beta' = -0.1879/181.8 - 0.00116 = -0.002193;
  alpha'' = 123.3*beta' - alpha' = -0.0826;
  beta'' = -0.0826/97.3 + 0.002193 = +0.001344;
  alpha''' = 5.8*beta'' + 0.0826 = +0.0904;
  beta''' = 0.0904/67.3 - 0.001344 = 0.
- Ray 2:
  gamma' = 700;
  delta' = 700/181.8 - 1 = 2.850;
  gamma'' = 123.3*2.85 - 700 = -348.5;
  delta'' = -348.5/97.3 - 2.85 = -6.431;
  gamma''' = 5.8*(-6.431) + 348.5 = 311.2;
  delta''' = 311.2/67.3 + 6.431 = 11.057.
- beta''' = 0 means the system is afocal, i.e. a telescope. The value d3 = 5.8 is evidently chosen to make it so: d3 = 1/phi4 + alpha''/beta'' = 67.3 - 61.46 = 5.84 (my derivation).
- delta''' = 11.06 is the angular magnification. As a check, alpha'''*delta''' = 0.9996, approximately 1 (unit determinant).

(3) APERTURE AND FIELD TABLE.
- Column 1 (52, 9.8, 4.3, 4.7) is the width of the axial pencil at each lens, for an objective aperture of 52 mm: 52*|alpha_k| = 9.77, 4.30, 4.70.
- Column 2 (51.0, 41.1, 33.3) is, I infer, the free diameters of lenses 2–4.
- Column 3 (250', 405, 368) is the field each lens admits, in arcminutes: 3437.75*D_k/|gamma_k| = 250.5', 405.4', 367.9'. The previous page's 246' (55.4/772.7) fits the same rule.
- So the second lens limits the field to about 4 deg 10'.

(4) ACHROMATISM OF MAGNIFICATION. The products are gamma_k*phi_k*alpha_k for k = 2, 3, 4:
- 3.85*(-0.188) = -0.72,
- -3.58*(-0.083) = +0.30,
- 4.63*(0.090) = +0.42,
- sum = 0.
Here gamma'/181.8 = 3.850, gamma''/97.3 = -3.582 and gamma'''/67.3 = 4.624. With a single glass for the eyepiece lenses, sum phi_k*alpha_k*gamma_k = 0 is the condition for no lateral colour (achromatism of the magnification). This trial satisfies it, whereas the previous page's trials left residuals of 0, -0.50 and -0.071.

(5) SCRATCH WORK. 38.0 - 5.8 = 32.2 compares the earlier third separation with the present one. The other small figures (16, 7, 2, 1; 127, 55, 111; 278.1, 56, 251) are not interpretable with certainty.

(6) PHYSICAL DATA. h = 719, h' = 112.6, h'' = 14.2 are evidently physical separations corresponding to the thin-lens values 700, 123.3, 5.8. 'Abstand des Auges 25 mm,1' is the eye distance (exit-pupil distance). In the thin-lens model the exit pupil lies gamma'''/delta''' = 28.1 behind the last lens. 25.1 presumably reflects real thicknesses or principal planes (unverified).

(7) CONTINUANT SENSITIVITY FORMULAS. Gauss's bracket (ab) denotes the continuant of the chain elements strictly between a and b. The chain is 1 = phi1, 2 = d1, 3 = phi2, 4 = d2, 5 = phi3, 6 = d3, 7 = phi4.
- Thus beta''' = -(08), delta''' = (18), beta' = (04), delta' = (14).
- The derivative of a continuant with respect to one element gives d beta'''/d(4) = (04)(48) = beta'*(48).
- The three-term continuant identity gives (04)(18) - (08)(14) = (48).
- Since beta''' = (08) = 0, this yields d beta'''/d d2 = beta'^2 * delta'''.
- Generally, for a separation mu: d beta'''/d mu = (0mu)^2 delta''' and d delta'''/d mu = (0mu)(1mu) delta'''.
- Numerical check (mine): d beta'''/d d2 = -0.024250*beta' and beta'*delta''' = -0.024248; d delta'''/d d2 = -0.06911 = beta'*delta'*delta'''.
- These give how afocality (focus) and magnification change when the separations are adjusted.

(8) Bottom right: 27.04, 9.2253 (possibly a logarithm), 71.1 — unexplained.
errors: No arithmetic errors found; all table values reproduce to rounding (delta''' recomputes as 11.055–11.057 depending on rounding of gamma''').
Eye distance 25.1 does not equal the thin-lens exit-pupil distance gamma'''/delta''' = 28.1; presumably it uses thick-lens data (h values), not verifiable from this page.
The line '= beta'(04)(18) - (08)(14)' is written loosely: the factor beta' should multiply the whole bracketed difference; the intended meaning is beta'[(04)(18)-(08)(14)].

results.what: Paraxial ray tracing of a 4-lens telescope with Gauss's system constants (alpha, beta, gamma, delta) and continuant recursion; afocal condition beta'''=0 fixing the eyepiece separation
results.modern_name: Gaussian (paraxial) optics / y-nu ray trace, ABCD matrices

results.what: Lateral-colour condition sum phi_k*y_k*ybar_k = 0 for a single-glass eyepiece
results.modern_name: Achromatism of magnification (transverse chromatic aberration, Seidel-type sum)
results.usually_credited_to: Huygens/Boscovich/Euler for eyepieces; general sum form 19th c. (Seidel 1856)

results.what: Field admitted by each lens = D_k/|gamma_k| (in arcminutes)
results.modern_name: Field-stop / vignetting analysis via chief-ray height

results.what: Sensitivities d beta'''/d mu = (0mu)^2 delta''', d delta'''/d mu = (0mu)(1mu) delta''' via continuant derivative and three-term continuant identity
results.modern_name: Differential (sensitivity) analysis of system matrix elements w.r.t. spacing; continuant identities
results.usually_credited_to: continuant identities: Euler; optical application: Gauss's continued-fraction dioptrics, later Möbius/Seidel

deep.surprise_reason: This is a practical telescope-design trial in Gauss's own published 1841 formalism. It includes an afocal condition, a lateral-colour balance, field limits and neat sensitivity formulas from continuant identities. These are elegant but elementary consequences of his known method.
